181 ## Latest Review Findings

182-

183-1. **Abort can leave partially committed persistence behind** — cancellation is checked before and after awaited writes, but the multi-step persistence path is not transactional or compensating, and the repositories still do not cancel the in-flight Prisma write itself. A timeout can therefore produce `workflow_timed_out` while earlier rows remain committed.

184- - Location: `src/domain/entities/services/write-initial-progression-values.ts:299-328`; `src/stately-studio/actors/write-attached-entity-records.ts:432-541`; `src/persistence/repositories/campaignEntityRepository.ts:115-172`

185-

186-2. **Abort listeners are retained after successful runs** — `raceWithAbort` registers abort listeners without removing them on normal resolve/reject, so repeated successful invocations can accumulate retained closures tied to the signal.

187- - Location: `src/stately-studio/actors/write-core-entity-record.ts:1-120`; `src/stately-studio/actors/write-attached-entity-records.ts:1-560`

182 ## Prior Review Findings

189-1. **Abort racing does not stop the underlying persistence work** — `raceWithAbort()` only rejects the wrapper promise. The persistence services (`createEntity`, `writeInitialFieldValues`, `writeInitialStatBlockValues*`, `writeInitialProgressionValues`, `writeInitialEntityRelations`) still do not accept an `AbortSignal`, so an invoke timeout can still leave the database write running after the workflow has already been canceled or blocked.

190- - Location: `src/stately-studio/actors/write-core-entity-record.ts:43-107`; `src/stately-studio/actors/write-attached-entity-records.ts:59-530`

191-

192-2. **Cancelled persistence may be reported as a write failure** — the create-machine invoke handlers still need to distinguish `AbortError` from real persistence failures, otherwise a timeout-driven abort can be misclassified and surface as the wrong terminal branch.

193- - Location: `src/stately-studio/createmachine.ts:1038-1211`

194-

195-1. `src/stately-studio/createmachine.ts:1007-1031` — the new `persist_create_drafts` timeout transitions the workflow to blocked, but the in-flight persistence invoke is not cancelled or made abort-aware. A slow write can still complete after the timeout path has already declared the flow blocked, which can leak a dangling write completion into an otherwise terminal state.

196-

197-1. `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/response/response-spec-builders.ts:23` contains a malformed `CampaignEntityData` import line that is syntactically invalid and blocks compilation.

198-2. `src/stately-studio/createmachine.ts` derives the post-review phase only from semantic workflow status, so a review edit that remains semantically complete can stay `review_ready` instead of reopening `dialogue_collecting` on the same `flowId`.

199-3. `src/stately-studio/createmachine.ts` transitions into `save_pending` and then immediately into persistence without a timeout or abort guard, so a hung write can stall the flow indefinitely.
